Vendored third-party code: Ed25519 signature verification
===========================================================

Source: https://github.com/orlp/ed25519 (a maintained fork of
floodyberry/ed25519-donna), commit as of 2024.

License: zlib license (see LICENSE in this directory). Copyright (c)
2015 Orson Peters <orsonpeters@gmail.com>.

Files vendored here: ed25519.h, fe.c/fe.h, fixedint.h, ge.c/ge.h,
precomp_data.h, sc.c/sc.h, sha512.c/sha512.h, verify.c, sign.c,
keypair.c.

The firmware/production code path in this subsystem
(Ed25519SignatureVerifier, DescriptorVerifier) only ever calls
`ed25519_verify` and its transitive dependencies (field/group/scalar
arithmetic and SHA-512); it never signs or generates keys, since a
device only ever needs to verify signatures produced elsewhere.

`sign.c` and `keypair.c` are additionally vendored (unmodified from
upstream) purely as *test tooling*: test/test_lora_ota_trust uses
`ed25519_create_keypair` + `ed25519_sign` to construct genuine,
real-crypto signed image descriptors for exercising
DescriptorVerifier's success and tamper-detection paths. This is a
real Ed25519 sign/verify round trip, not a mock -- it deliberately
avoids "pretending" a fake stand-in is cryptographic. The upstream
seed-generation (`seed.c`, OS RNG) and key-exchange (`key_exchange.c`,
`add_scalar.c`) sources are still intentionally NOT vendored, since
tests supply their own fixed, deterministic 32-byte seeds and have no
need for X25519 key exchange.

This code is unmodified from upstream except for path-qualified
`#include` directives where needed for this repository's build layout.
Correctness is pinned by the RFC 8032 known-answer test vectors in
test/test_lora_ota_trust.
